note: Hand-curated names for common ingredients. Each entry points at one USDA SR Legacy record (fdcId) and form, or at a model. usdaDescription is copied byte-for-byte from the USDA record.

Caster sugar has finer crystals than granulated. USDA has no record for it, so the granulated sugar figure is used and may run a few percent off.
Demerara is not turbinado; USDA lists only turbinado, used here as the nearest record.
USDA lists one molasses record; blackstrap and light molasses differ slightly.

Fresh coriander (UK, AU) is cilantro. Coriander seed is a separate ingredient.

aliases.usdaDescription: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw

Rocket (UK, AU) is arugula.

aliases.note: Raw. Mashed sweet potato has its own entry.

aliases.usdaDescription: Sweet potato, cooked, boiled, without skin
aliases.note: Boiled without skin, then mashed.

aliases.usdaDescription: Potatoes, mashed, home-prepared, whole milk and butter added
aliases.note: USDA record is home-prepared with whole milk and butter, so the figure includes them.
Polenta is coarse cornmeal. The record is fine degermed cornmeal, and a coarse grind packs a little differently, so treat the figure as approximate.
Linseed (UK) is flaxseed. Ground flaxseed has its own entry.

aliases.usdaDescription: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained, rinsed in tap water
aliases.note: Canned, drained and rinsed. Home-cooked chickpeas weigh a little more per cup.

aliases.usdaDescription: Beans, black, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
aliases.note: Boiled without salt. Canned black beans, drained, come close. Dried black beans have their own entry.
USDA has one short-grain white rice record, uncooked. Sushi rice (JP) and pudding rice (UK) are short-grain varieties.

Pasta, cooked, enriched, without added salt

aliases.usdaDescription: Pasta, cooked, enriched, without added salt
aliases.note: Loosely packed strands. Linguine and other long pasta are close.

aliases.usdaDescription: Oats (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)
aliases.note: USDA lists whole raw oats (groats). Steel-cut oats are the same grain cut into pieces, so the figure is close but approximate.
USDA record is Deglet Noor. Medjool dates are larger and softer, so weigh them.
Dried Zante currants, the baking kind. Fresh red and black currants are a different fruit.
Raw sweet cherries, pitted.
Raw whole berries. Dried cranberries have their own entry.

aliases.usdaDescription: Soymilk, original and vanilla, with added calcium, vitamins A and D
aliases.note: Soya milk (UK, AU) is soy milk. The record is original and vanilla soy milk with added calcium and vitamins.

aliases.usdaDescription: Beverages, almond milk, sweetened, vanilla flavor, ready-to-drink
aliases.note: The sweetened vanilla record is used because the unsweetened record reads 262 g per cup, too heavy for a thin milk. USDA lists a cup of the vanilla record at 240 g, the same as water.

aliases.usdaDescription: Nuts, coconut cream, raw (liquid expressed from grated meat)
aliases.note: USDA lists raw coconut cream at exactly 240 g per cup. Canned coconut cream is thicker, so treat the figure as approximate.

Diamond Crystal and Morton kosher salt differ by about 1.7 times per teaspoon. This is the Morton figure.

Labels give Greek yogurt servings as a nominal fraction of a cup (170 g as 3/4 cup), which reads about 9 percent lower than USDA plain yogurt (1.036 g/mL). For a measured cup, "plain yogurt" is the better figure.
Kosher salt weighs about 1.7 times more per teaspoon in Morton than in Diamond Crystal. Name the brand.
Reference density 0.9982 g/mL at 20 C, scaled for temperature with the Choi-Okos water polynomial.
UK single cream is at least 18 percent milk fat. Density comes from the dairy model.
Whipping cream (UK, Canada) is 35 percent milk fat or more. Density comes from the dairy model at 35 percent; pass fatPercent for another figure.
UK double cream is at least 48 percent milk fat, above the 36.08 percent top of the USDA records the dairy model was fitted to, so the result is an extrapolation.
